name: disorders of puberty overview
title: Disorders of puberty pathway: puberty before 8 in girls or 9 in boys is precocious, and splits into two normal variants (isolated premature thelarche and pubarche) and, by random luteinizing hormone, central (GnRH dependent) or peripheral (GnRH independent) precocious puberty; no signs by 13 in girls or 14 in boys is delayed, and splits into constitutional delay (delayed bone age), primary hypogonadism (LH and FSH high: Turner, Klinefelter) and secondary hypogonadism (LH and FSH low: brain causes, Kallmann); each column gives causes and clues, investigations, and outcome or treatment

root.title: Is puberty too EARLY or too LATE, and is the brain driving it?
lines: normal onset: GIRLS 8–13 y (1st sign thelarche, breast budding) · BOYS 9–14 y (1st sign testicular volume > 3 mL)

groups.title: PRECOCIOUS puberty: too EARLY
lines: onset BEFORE 8 y in girls · BEFORE 9 y in boys

groups.title: DELAYED puberty: too LATE
lines: NO pubertal signs by 13 y in girls · 14 y in boys
~absent or incomplete puberty at 2.5 SD above the population mean

tiers.title: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) dependent?
lines: random luteinizing hormone (LH): more useful than FSH for onset

tiers.title: Bone age, LH and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH)?
lines: sex steroids (estradiol / testosterone) LOW in both hypogonadisms

head: h
Isolated premature thelarche
normal VARIANT
breast development only
clue: very low-grade estrogenization of the vaginal mucosa only

head: h
Isolated premature pubarche
normal VARIANT
pubic hair only: ADRENAL
inv: Tanner-staged, but NOT a marker for the ONSET of puberty
tx: • later polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) in girls

head: h
Central precocious puberty (CPP)
GnRH DEPENDENT
early activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis
LH/FSH ↑ · sex steroids ↑
clue: • commonest cause of precocious puberty in girls
• only the timing or tempo is abnormal
< 50% idiopathic → careful central nervous system (CNS) assessment
chronic sex steroid exposure → HPG on
inv: ~• low LH alone is insensitive: LH is PULSATILE
• LH response exaggerated: peak LH > 5 mIU/L confirms
if a CNS cause is suspected: BOYS need careful CNS work-up
tx: • DOWN-REGULATES pituitary receptors → removes the PULSATILE pattern, stops puberty
1 · arrest puberty, incl. menses · 2 · slow bone maturation, delay epiphyseal closure → final height · 3 · psychosocial well-being

head: h
Peripheral precocious puberty (PPP)
GnRH INDEPENDENT
LH/FSH ↓ · sex steroids ↑
clue: testosterone from elsewhere (e.g. adrenal): acne, pubic hair, ↑ stretched penile length, fast growth and bone maturation
• congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH): cortisol ↓, ± salt wasting
inv: 2 · May still need GnRH STIMULATION test
a low random LH does not exclude CPP

head: h
Constitutional delay of growth and puberty (CDGP)
normal VARIANT
COMMONEST cause of delayed puberty, especially in boys
h
Primary hypogonadism
hypergonadotropic: the GONAD fails
LH/FSH ↑ · sex steroids ↓
tx: • autoimmune: thyroid, celiac, type 1 diabetes, hearing, metabolic syndrome

head: h
Secondary hypogonadism
hypogonadotropic: the BRAIN fails
LH/FSH ↓ · sex steroids ↓
inv: if a CNS cause is suspected
tx: Replace sex steroid · treat the cause

panels.title: Normal puberty
items: GIRLS: thelarche → growth spurt (Tanner 2–3) → pubarche → menarche · 15% have pubarche first
breast Tanner 2 10.3 y · pubic hair 11.2 y · menarche 12.7 y, 2.5 y after thelarche
BOYS: testes > 3 mL → penis → pubarche → growth spurt (Tanner 3–4, testes 10–12 mL) → voice → muscle → facial hair
boys' average onset 11.5 ± 1.3 y · later spurt = taller final height

panels.title: Assess every child
items: history: timing and progression of milestones · growth spurt? · CNS symptoms · medications, radiation
family: parental heights · parents' age at puberty
exam: plot height and weight · Tanner stages · CNS signs · dysmorphism · skin marks

panels.title: Investigations
items: random LH (> 0.3 suggests CPP) · estradiol / testosterone · bone age · thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH)
± karyotype for DELAYED puberty · pelvic ultrasound
± LHRH STIMULATION test: gold standard for PRECOCIOUS · MRI head if CNS suspected

panels.title: Before starting an LHRH analogue, ask
items: how early is onset? similar to the family pattern?
predicted adult height below the 3rd percentile or below parental target?
psychosocial impact on the child, parents and peers

panels.title: Testes size splits a virilized boy
items: BOTH testes ≥ 4 mL: CENTRAL, since LH drives Leydig cells
virilized with testes < 3 mL: PERIPHERAL source of testosterone
one testis larger: Leydig cell tumour
